_real_world.class: F-35C Lightning II low-observable (5th-generation stealth) radar cross section
_real_world.variant_scope: F-35C carrier variant, clean internal-weapons-bay loadout, frontal aspect within the ~30-40 deg nose cone
public_equipment: F-35 publicly cited frontal RCS 0.001-0.005 m2 class ('golf ball' sized), multiple public sources (GlobalSecurity.org, Military Embedded Systems); rear aspect explicitly noted as significantly larger due to unshielded engine exhaust/nozzle

_provenance.modeling_note: F-35C is the optional CVW-8 branch (count 0 in the 2025-26 baseline). Multiple independent public sources converge on a frontal RCS in the 0.001-0.005 m2 class for the F-35 family (golf-ball-sized, an order of magnitude larger than the F-22's reported 0.0001-0.0005 m2); the higher end of that band (0.005) is used here as a conservative, non-optimistic estimate since exact classified figures are not public and vary by source/aspect-angle methodology. Not reusing the repo's existing LO_Fighter_RCS (0.01 frontal): that generic profile is 2x higher than the sourced F-35 class figure and does not capture the specifically-documented rear-aspect weakness. Public sources explicitly and consistently flag that F-35's rear-aspect RCS is much larger than its frontal aspect because the engineers did not fully shield the exhaust nozzle for cost reasons (GlobalSecurity.org, Military Embedded Systems); rear_rcs is therefore set as a clear outlier above the other four aspects, unlike a typical LO airframe's rear/frontal ratio, to reflect this specific, repeatedly-sourced design tradeoff. side/top/bottom_rcs have no quantified public figures and are engineering_estimate proxies scaled from frontal_rcs using the repo LO_Fighter_RCS's own frontal:side:top/bottom ratio pattern (0.01:0.5:1.0, i.e. side~50x frontal, top/bottom~100x frontal for a low-observable design, since large flat/curved planform areas dominate off-nose returns even on stealth shapes), scaled down proportionally to this record's lower frontal baseline.

rcs.frontal_rcs.note: 0.005 m2, the higher (more conservative) end of the widely-cited public 0.001-0.005 m2 class range for F-35 frontal RCS; exact classified figure not public

rcs.side_rcs.note: scaled from frontal_rcs using the repo LO_Fighter_RCS's frontal:side ratio (~1:50); no public F-35 side-aspect figure

rcs.rear_rcs.note: engineering_estimate set as a deliberate outlier (100x frontal) reflecting the specifically-sourced, repeatedly-documented design tradeoff that F-35's rear aspect is much larger than its frontal aspect due to an unshielded engine exhaust nozzle; the exact rear-aspect number is not public, but the qualitative severity of the gap is well sourced

rcs.top_rcs.note: scaled from frontal_rcs using the repo LO_Fighter_RCS's frontal:top ratio (~1:100); no public figure

rcs.bottom_rcs.note: scaled from frontal_rcs using the repo LO_Fighter_RCS's frontal:bottom ratio (~1:100); no public figure
